written: 2026-10-02 14:13 +05, before any measurement of the arms it adds; AFTER the v1 ResNet18 INT8 arms were recorded and seen (evals-v2/resnet18-int8: axe and naive within 1 point of rtn down to P=25, 64.7/62.3 at P=24, at most 3.0 at P<=23; sat.wP within 1 point down to 19). The added arms are therefore post hoc and are reported as exploratory, separately from the v1 primary comparison, which is unchanged.
reason: AXE (like OPTQ/GPFQ) keeps the quantizer scales fixed and moves only the integers (arXiv:2409.17092v1, Sec. 2.3: 'in the PTQ setting, one often assumes the quantizer parameters ... are fixed'). With the per-channel scale s_c fixed, the code-unit bound sum(q>0) <= L is a bound on the real-valued weights, sum(w>0) <= s_c*L, so the network function itself must shrink; the QAT methods A2Q/A2Q+ instead learn the scale together with the weights. The added arms ask whether an accumulator-aware per-channel scale, which meets the same guarantee by coarsening the channel's grid instead of shrinking its weights, moves the narrowest lossless P. They are a stated departure from AXE, not AXE.

added_arms.rescale-P<P>: data-free. For every output channel c of every MAC node: k_c = the smallest factor >= 1 (bisection, 60 halvings, on the interval [1, 2*max|w/s_c|+1]) such that the nearest-rounded codes round((w/s_c)/k_c), clipped to the codebook, meet the v1 bound beta_c <= L and -alpha_c <= L with L = floor((2^(P-1)-1)/(2^N-1)); feasibility is monotone in k because |round(x/k)| is non-increasing in k. Codes q_c = round((w/s_c)/k_c); deployed scale s_c*k_c (float32). k_c = 1 (codes = rtn) for channels that already meet the bound.
added_arms.axers-P<P>:
AXE-OPTQ (v1 'axe' method, unchanged code, same order, damping, calibration, soft and hard constraint at the same P) run on the grid of the rescale-P

scales s_c*k_c, i.e. on the weights (w/s_c)/k_c in the new code units. The hard clip guarantees the bound whatever OPTQ's error feedback does.

unchanged_for_the_added_arms: activation recipe and scales, B2 empirical bias correction after the integers are fixed, the bound, bound_holds, the engine certificate on the replaced integers (scales do not enter it), the 32-image integer prefix check, evaluation on all 1000 screen images in the B2 simulator, both tie rules, the paired statistics and the derived-width rule (reference: rtn for rescale, rtn and optq for axers). Records also store, per arm, the sha256 of the factors k and per-layer summaries (max k, fraction of channels with k > 1, mean log2 k).
cases_and_widths: resnet18-int8 P 27..14 and resnet18-int6 P 23..11 (the v1 grids).
documentation_of_existing_departures: the paper applies graph (weight) equalization (Nagel et al. 2019) before calibrating scales (App. C, 'Quantization Process'); the B2 default recipe has none and this wave's rule 12 forbids cross-layer-equalization arms, so no arm of this lane uses it. It is an adapted part of every arm and is listed as such in the report (v1 did not list it).

weight integers of rtn, optq and the key arms are stored per the v1 storage rule by re-running those arms with --save-codes into a scratch folder, checking that weight_codes_sha256 and the per-image readouts equal the sealed evals-v2 records (determinism check), and then copying the codes files to artifacts/experiment_b2_axe/codes-v2/<case>/<arm>.codes.npz with a sealed manifest.
budget: about 35 additional GPU minutes (rescale ~20 s, axers ~60 s per arm); same gpu_run limits.
